newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt prices mostly lower, spreads mixed.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt prices mostly lower, spreads mixed.

text.p: Emerging market bonds ended mostly lower after a day of listless U.S. trading, traders said.
Spreads were mostly wider, with Venezuela papers giving back the bulk of Tuesday's gains, they said.
Market participants paused because of the uncertainties of of U.S. interest rates, they noted.
With the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond hovering near 7.0 percent, a 25-basis-point increase in federal funds rate has already been priced in the market.
But before the rate hike becomes official, trading in the Treasuries and the spread products is expected to remain turbulent, said a trader with a U.S. investment house.
Mexico Brady bonds barely reacted to a clutch of bullish news that sent the bolsa soaring.

The 28-day Cetes rate in Tuesday's auction fell to 21.70 percent from last week's 23.71 percent and Mexcio's National Statistics Institute reported on Wednesday that open unemployment for February declined to 4.2 percent, down from 6.3 percent in the year-ago period.

Richard Segal, director of emerging market fixed income research at Santander Investments, said the "open unemployment" number, which leaves out a large sector of the economy, is often considered as a not very reliable indicator by fixed income professionals.
A traders noted that the nervousness over U.S. rates affected the heavily collateralized Mexican Bradies, noting also that U.S. investors had lately favored Latin equities over stocks.
